title: v-if Versus v-show
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of v-if Versus v-show in a Vue 3 application.

content.intro: This lesson studies v-if Versus v-show within Directives and Rendering Patterns. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Selecting a directive carefully affects lifecycle, rendering cost, security, and maintainability.

content_blocks.title: v-if Versus v-show: Measure before optimizing

content_blocks.caption: Performance workflow: measure a reproducible baseline, optimize the observed bottleneck, and repeat the same test.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Directives add reactive behavior to elements, while custom directives package focused DOM interactions when a component or composable is not a better fit. This lesson focuses on v-if Versus v-show. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Element creation and removal
items.text: For Element creation and removal, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: CSS-based visibility
items.text: For CSS-based visibility, keep the visual rule in CSS where possible and bind reactive values only when state genuinely changes presentation. Check responsive behavior and reduced-motion preferences; animation should communicate state rather than block interaction.

items.title: Performance considerations
items.text: For Performance considerations, measure first and optimize the constrained resource rather than guessing. Compare before/after behavior, keep stable identity for rendered lists, and verify that an optimization does not make the code harder to maintain.

items.title: Choosing the right directive
items.text: For Choosing the right directive, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.

content_blocks.expected_output: Both messages become visually hidden when toggled off, but v-if creates/removes while v-show changes display.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run as App.vue. Inspect the DOM before and after toggling to compare the directives.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through v-if Versus v-show with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “CSS-based visibility”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Directives add reactive behavior to elements, while custom directives package focused DOM interactions when a component or composable is not a better fit. For v-if Versus v-show, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.
